artworks.title: Plate Number 380. Carpenter, sawing a board
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a sequential series of using a saw. The image consists of multiple frames arranged in a grid, illustrating the action of a person performing woodwork with a saw. Each frame captures a different moment in the motion, showing a detailed progression of the activity. The background and setting suggest an industrial or workshop environment, with wooden structures and tools visible. The series is likely a study of movement, emphasizing the physical exertion and technique involved in handling the tool. The overall composition and repetitive layout highlight the precision and rhythm in the act of sawing.

artworks.title: Plate Number 400. Emptying a bucket of water
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequential study of an individual carrying and throwing a bucket of water. The image consists of multiple frames arranged in a grid format, capturing the motion in incremental stages. Each frame shows a slightly different position as the person progresses from walking to throwing water. The background features a plain setting that suggests an outdoor environment with a simple structure. The sequential nature of the photographs showcases an experiment in capturing motion and the fluidity of movement, providing a dynamic study of motion over a series of moments frozen in time.

artworks.title: Plate Number 401. Emptying a bucket of water
artworks.description: This is a series of black and white photographs showing an individual interacting with a bucket outdoors. Each frame captures a different moment in the motion. The background varies between a grid-like pattern and outdoor structures. The images focus on the physical dynamics of using a bucket, including the flow of water in the middle row. The set provides insight into movement and photography.

artworks.title: Plate Number 428. Woman disrobing another
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of movement studies with drapery. The image is composed of multiple sequential frames arranged in two rows capturing a study in movement and the interaction with a piece of cloth. The top row depicts actions involving wrapping, lifting, and adjusting the drapery, while the bottom row shows similar poses from a different angle. The arrangement of frames conveys fluid motion and interaction between figures and fabric, emphasizing both figurative and form aspects. The background is simple and minimalistic, focusing the viewer's attention on the detailed motion and transitions.

artworks.title: Plate Number 435. Ironing clothes
artworks.description: This image features multiple frames organized in a grid, depicting a sequence of actions. The setting is outdoors with a wooden floor and a fence or wall in the background. The frames show various objects, including a table covered with a cloth, a small basket or bucket, and a cloth item. The sequence demonstrates continuous movement and changes in posture while interacting with the objects. The focus is on capturing the dynamics of the activity.

artworks.title: Plate Number 480. Child walking and crawling up stairs
artworks.description: This is a series of images capturing a young figure stepping up onto a platform. The composition features two rows of frames showing the various stages of the movement. The background is a horizontally striped wall.

artworks.title: Plate Number 512. Contortions on the rings
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence of movements involving gymnastics rings. The image comprises two rows, each row containing multiple frames that capture different stages of an acrobatic routine performed with rings. Each frame appears to transition smoothly from the previous one, emphasizing motion and flexibility as the acrobat moves through a sequence of poses. The photographic series captures the detailed muscle definition and the balanced positions held on the rings. The background features a grid pattern in the top row and a darker, draped setting in the bottom row, providing contrast to accentuate the subject's movements.

artworks.title: Plate Number 520. A-C: Wrestling. D: Sparring without gloves
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a sequence of two figures engaged in an activity. The image consists of smaller photographs arranged in rows, capturing different poses and stages of a physical encounter. The figures are shown in varied positions suggesting movement, physical interaction, and balance, showcasing the human form in motion. The monochrome photographs highlight the contrasts and contours of the figures against a simple background, capturing the essence of dynamic movement without interpretation.

artworks.title: Plate Number 522. A: Jumping. B: Handspring. C, D: Somersault. E: Springing over a man's back
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a series of motion studies. The image contains multiple frames arranged in a grid, capturing sequences of dynamic movements. Each row depicts different sets of motion, showcasing a figure transitioning through various acrobatic and athletic poses including jumping, carrying, and contorting. The use of monochrome offers a classic and scientific look to the study, resembling early motion photography experimentation and emphasizing the precise capturing of movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 523. A: Striking a blow. B, E: Throwing a disk. C, F: Heaving a 75-lb. stone. D: Throwing a ball
artworks.description: This is a series of black and white photographs depicting a figure in motion with a discus. The grid arrangement captures the detailed sequence of athletic movement. Each frame shows progressive shots of the figure in motion, against a dark background. The images focus on the movement and contours of the figure as it performs the discus throw action. The emphasis is on the dynamics of human movement and subtle shifts in posture, showcasing different phases of the athletic gesture in detail. The sequence highlights human kinetics and the form of the athletic body in motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 524. A: Throwing water from a bucket. B: Descending a step. C: Ascending a step. D: Playing lawn tennis
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a grid of images depicting movement. The sequence captures a figure performing various actions like pouring from a bucket, holding a garment, stepping on a block, and gesturing upward. The grayscale tones emphasize the contrasts and outline the figure's shape and form in motion against a dark background.

artworks.title: Plate Number 538. Double amputation of thighs, boy. A: Moving forward. B: Getting on chair. C: Getting down from chair
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence showing movement across a chair. The image consists of multiple frames arranged in a grid-like format, each capturing a progressive movement over a chair. The background appears simple and nondescript, focusing the attention on the action taking place in each frame. The progression shows subtle shifts in posture and balance as if the subject is performing an exercise or a task involving the chair. Each frame is labeled at the bottom with numbers, indicating steps in the sequence.

artworks.title: Plate Number 570. "Hansel" hauling
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse in motion. The image shows a grid of black and white sequential photographs displaying the step-by-step movement of the horse as it walks. The panels depict the gradual progression of the horse's gait, showcasing the shifts in its posture and leg positions. The background is plain to draw attention to the horse's movement. Each frame is numbered systematically, highlighting the motion study aspect of the series. The horse is wearing harness gear, indicating it may be used for work or study in a controlled setting.

artworks.title: Plate Number 599. "Dusel" trotting, bareback
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a sequence of a horse walking. It features frames in two rows, detailing each moment of the horse's stride. The first row shows the horse from the front, and the second from behind. The frames highlight the motion of the horse's legs as it walks, against a plain background. The sequence captures the natural movement of the horse's limbs as it walks.

artworks.title: Plate Number 647. "Pandora" jumping a hurdle, bareback; rider nude
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse jumping a barrier. It shows a series of black and white frames capturing the motion of the horse as it approaches, jumps over, and lands after clearing the barrier. The images are arranged in two rows, with the top row showing side views of the action and the bottom row providing rear views. The horse looks muscular and powerful. The setting appears to be outdoors, with fencing in the background suggesting an enclosed area for animal movement study. The sequential layout of the photographs emphasizes the dynamic motion of jumping.

artworks.title: Plate Number 691. Fallow deer, doe galloping and kid jumping
artworks.description: This is a series of 12 black and white frames showing a deer in motion against a fenced background on a dirt ground. The frames capture the deer transitioning through stages of running and leaping, showcasing the animal's movement. The sequence highlights the deer's agility and grace, offering a detailed look at its gait and body positioning. The frames are presented in a systematic format, providing a detailed analysis of the deer's kinetic form.

artworks.title: Plate Number 700. Buffalo galloping
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a bison captured in sequential motion. The image consists of a series of frames arranged in a grid, showing the various stages of a bison walking. Each frame captures the bison from a side profile, showcasing the different positions of its legs and body as it moves forward. The background is minimal, highlighting the bison's movement and form. The photograph effectively captures the essence of motion, providing a detailed study of the animal's gait and anatomy.

artworks.title: Plate Number 735. Two elephants walking
artworks.description: This is a photograph of two elephants walking away. The image is divided into multiple frames, resembling a sequential series of the elephants walking side by side. Each frame shows slight differences in the movement of their trunks, tails, and legs as they proceed forward. The elephants have rough, textured skin, and their large bodies dominate each segment of the image. In the background, there are barriers, possibly fencing, with some trees and structures suggesting an outdoor setting. The lighting appears neutral, highlighting the elephants from their rear view, capturing the motion of their strides.

artworks.title: Plate Number 764. Fish hawk flying
artworks.description: This is a series of images showing the sequential motion of a bird in flight. The top row displays the bird from a side view with flapping wings in different flight phases, separated by vertical grid lines. The bottom row shows the bird from a front-facing angle with wings in varying positions. The bird is captured against a textured grid pattern background, emphasizing its detailed flight motion and structure.

artworks.title: Plate Number 769. American eagle flying
artworks.description: Photograph showing a series of images of an eagle in flight. The grid composed of smaller panels captures sequential moments as the eagle maneuvers. The bird's wingspan is prominently displayed, with its wings in different stages of flapping. The black and white photographs have a classic look. The background is plain to emphasize the motion of the eagle. This collection of images represents an early study of movement, capturing the grace and power of the eagle in flight.

artworks.title: Plate Number 781. Chickens scared by a torpedo
artworks.description: This is a series of frames showing pigeons flying across a brick alleyway. The frames capture the motion of the birds with their wings in different positions. The background shows dust or smoke-like plumes. The series freezes a moment of the birds taking flight, showcasing their physical movement.

artworks.title: West Wind
artworks.medium: mezzotint in black with chine collé on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Frank B. Bristow, 1968)
artworks.description: The image displays a landscape with an expansive view of land leading to distant mountains. The horizon is positioned lower in the composition, emphasizing the sky above. Silhouettes of trees and mountains are visible along the horizon. The brushstrokes are soft, capturing the quality of light and shadow. The color palette is monochromatic or sepia-toned, giving a timeless quality to the image. The clouds in the sky are voluminous, casting shadows. Light suggests either early morning or late afternoon, seen by the illumination on the water in the distance.

artworks.title: Bay window on the Hall, Speke, Lancashire
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.description: This is a painting of a grand, richly decorated interior room with a bay window. The room is adorned with wooden paneling, intricate carvings, and large red drapes. A warm fire burns in a large fireplace to the right, casting a warm glow in the room. The floor features a black and white checkered pattern with a red carpet partially covering it. A richly attired woman is seated by the fireplace with a book in her lap, and another figure stands near the bay windows at the back, gazing outside. A child is depicted with an open book, engaged in reading or looking at its pages. This is in the style of Samuel Prout, known for his detailed and atmospheric portrayals of architectural interiors.

artworks.title: Title Page
artworks.medium: pen and black ink over graphite with applied wove paper on paperboard
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a catalogue cover for the Corcoran Gallery of Art. The image shows a sketch with the words "The Corcoran Gallery of Art Catalogue" and handwritten notes in cursive. The drawing includes a stone lion statue on a plinth, set next to steps leading up to tall columns. On the steps are a man and a young girl in Victorian-era clothing. The man holds a top hat and wears a tailcoat while the girl holds a parasol and wears a long-sleeved dress and wide-brimmed hat. An annotation showing "4 5/8" is included underneath the sketch.
